sourceInformation.genre: Sandbox action RPG with block building, crafting and town building
sourceInformation.perspective: Isometric third person (three-quarter view optional in Settings), camera turns in 90 degree steps
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.2 (TileMap, Humanoid and Blob rigs, canvas lighting), plain JavaScript, AI Hub session client 1.4.0, Node and Playwright 1.63.0 for tests; single HTML file, no CDN
sourceInformation.artDirection: Engine-native HD pixel look; every block is a stitched fabric patch, sewing-themed tools and monsters, stitched quilt UI panels
sourceInformation.animation: Engine Humanoid and Blob rigs with E.MOVES, tweens and game.script cutscenes, boss telegraphs
sourceInformation.audio: All code: chip sfx voices, original songs on the engine synth, Animalese formant voice synth per speaker; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub session protocol v1, ghost mode: Quilting Bee round for 1-4 builders (passes the hub harness); playable solo from the title
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Node scripts (game.advance, game.debug) including a full scripted playthrough, plus Playwright checks for real keyboard, mouse, fake DualSense, UI screens and the hub harness
sourceInformation.research: Read the engine handoff docs, the AI Hub protocol and the plan; no outside research
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; browser unknown

testingFeedback: About 14 issues were caught by tests, plus several visual ones found in screenshots.
3 were critical: a quest director crash, the final boss never spawning if a cutscene was active, and the KO dialog freezing the respawn.
The scripted headless playthrough from the first block to defeating Gnarlgrim, and the fake-DualSense browser test.
Static screenshots taken mid-cutscene, which mostly showed popups mid-queue.
engineFeedback: TileMap with wall heights, cutaway walls and the Humanoid and Blob rigs make an isometric block world cheap; headless game.advance made real testing easy.
Yes: weapon kinds are swords only, Dialog had no per-letter hook, and TileMap holds one type per column so mixed-material walls need a type per material and height.
Block column editing, room detection, A* with breaker costs, crafting and notions, town and Cheer, siege and bosses, UI panels, prompt glyphs and the Animalese synth.
Stacking blocks on a heightmap, and making every screen work equally for pad, keyboard and mouse.
Added a Dialog onLetter(ch, index) hook so the Animalese voice can play per letter.
True voxel layers in TileMap (several blocks per column with different materials and overhangs).
promptFeedback: The plan gave a clear structure, content tables and a test philosophy that made the build predictable.
The plan assumes a custom voxel renderer and many systems (Patterns, Builder's Eye, shared world) far beyond one session.
Scope: fitting a full vertical slice with online play, attract mode and dev tools into one build.
A smaller must-have list, with the plan sections marked optional or cut-able.

aiHub.name: Dragon Quilt Builders
aiHub.tagline: Stitch a town, unpick a dragon's knot
aiHub.description: A sandbox action RPG where you break blocks, craft, build rooms for quirky residents and defend Thimbleton from the Knotted army. Includes a 3-minute Quilting Bee co-op defence round.
aiHub.controls: Move: stick/WASD. Swing: square/click. Place: triangle/right click. Talk: circle/F. Jump: cross/Space. Satchel: Create/Tab.
